senses.gloss: f., pl. טוּרְמִיאוֹת, טוּרְמִיּוֹת (turma, τούρμη) turma, a squadron of horse; in gen. division of an army. Y. Sot. VIII, beg. 22ᵇ (ref. to Ps. XVIII, 13) כנגד טומיות שלהם (corr. acc.) corresponding to their (the enemy’s) squadrons.
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 160">Yalk. Sam. 160</cite>; Mekh. B’shall. s. 2 <he>תּוּרְמִיּוֹת</he>. Ib. <he>ת׳ ת׳ של מה״ש</he> troops of angels. Ib. (ref. to <he>סֵעַ</he>: <cite ref="Exodus 14:10">Ex. XIV, 10</cite>) <he>נעשו … ת׳ ת׳ כאיש אחד</he> they all formed squadrons marching like one man; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 230">Yalk. Ex. 230</cite> <he>ט׳ ט׳</he>.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 230">Ib.</cite> <he>מכאן … מתנהגות ת׳</he> from here (the Egyptian warfare) the governments learned to form squadrons; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 230">Yalk. Ex. 230</cite> <he>ט׳</he>.
